#### STATE CAPTURE 2.O

# Cat Matlala’s plans for political control followed the State Capture playbook

Vusimuzi ‘Cat’ Matlala’s appearance in court on Wednesday underscores what the Madlanga Commission is revealing — capture begins by cultivating political insiders who unlock the machinery of government.

[![Ferial Haffajee](https://cdn.dailymaverick.co.za/i/5wM4-8j9Qq_CZBYMFnEuit2fSyo=/450x0/smart/file/authors/64816591545251603.jpg)](https://www.dailymaverick.co.za/author/ferialhaffajee/?dm_source=article-author-bar&dm_medium=link&dm_campaign=author_profile "Ferial Haffajee")

By [Ferial Haffajee](https://www.dailymaverick.co.za/author/ferialhaffajee/?dm_source=article-author-bar&dm_medium=link&dm_campaign=author_profile "Ferial Haffajee")

25 Mar 2026

[](https://www.google.com/preferences/source?q=dailymaverick.co.za)[](https://news.google.com/search?q=Daily+Maverick)

![Fer-Cat-Paul](https://cdn.dailymaverick.co.za/attachments/orphans/EdwinSodispartywithMatlala_769114.jpg) _Illustrative image: Paul Mashatile’s spokesperson Keith Khoza with Vusimuzi ‘Cat’ Matalala at Edwin Sodi’s 50th birthday party. (Photo: Supplied / News24 | Illustration: Kevin Momberg)_

*   Dive Deeper
*   Speed Read
*   Summary
*   Listen

Dive Deeper

As Vusimusi “Cat” Matlala appeared in court on Wednesday, 25 March 2026, testimony at the Madlanga Commission has shown how tender kingpins cultivate politicians – with access, luxury and cash – to capture the state from the inside.

The image below represents the potential risk of the criminalisation of the state, first exposed by [News24](https://www.news24.com/investigations/mashatiles-man-anc-leaders-party-with-cat-matlala-at-corruption-accused-sodis-mansion-20250730-1151) and now being ventilated at the Madlanga Commission of Inquiry into Criminality, Political Interference and Corruption in the Criminal Justice System.

![Fer-Cat-Paul](https://cdn.dailymaverick.co.za/i/DvYzDA809qCFcpnGPhkhtX98tvw=/200x100/smart/filters:strip_exif()/file/attachments/orphans/header_f_wide_809735.jpeg "Paul Mashatile’s spokesperson Keith Khoza with Vusimuzi ‘Cat’ Matalala at Edwin Sodi's 50th birthday party. (Photo: Supplied / News24)")

Paul Mashatile’s spokesperson Keith Khoza with Vusimuzi ‘Cat’ Matalala at Edwin Sodi's 50th birthday party. (Photo: Supplied / News24)

In it, the tender kingpin Edwin Sodi, a key figure in State Capture networks, is enjoying his 50th birthday party.

At his table is Matlala, the 49-year-old now in jail on charges including attempted murder and on Wednesday charged with 12 others for fraud, corruption and money-laundering in relation to a R360-million police tender riddled with malfeasance.

[

FOR CONTEXT

‘Dirty dozen’ cops in the dock for ‘Cat’ Matlala R360m tender fraud scandal

March 25, 2026

![](https://cdn.dailymaverick.co.za/i/4v6KBcax5-7yVPLuAoFYPEmHNxw=/450x0/smart/file/attachments/orphans/WFD_7289_106507.jpg)

](https://www.dailymaverick.co.za/article/2026-03-25-dirty-dozen-cops-in-the-dock-for-cat-matlala-r360m-tender-fraud-scandal/)

Standing near Sodi is Keith Khoza, the political adviser to Deputy President Paul Mashatile. Many other politicians attended the party, according to this report.

What the table reveals is how close tender kingpins got to the political kingdom. This week, the Madlanga Commission heard a final day of testimony from Sergeant Fannie Nkosi, the police bagman who was a [lynchpin of the “Big Five” cartel](https://www.dailymaverick.co.za/article/2026-03-22-sergeant-fannie-nkosi-information-and-kickback-peddler-between-big-five-and-saps/).

The Big Five are the crime lords named by KwaZulu-Natal police commissioner Nhlanhla Mkhwanazi in July 2025, exposing infiltration of the criminal justice system.

Sodi can’t afford another party like this one after SARS tax compliance actions against him; he is also facing longstanding charges related to alleged [corruption](https://www.dailymaverick.co.za/article/2026-02-18-court-orders-moroadi-cholota-to-stand-trd-trial-with-magashule-in-r255m-asbestos/) in a R255-million asbestos roofing contract in the Free State.

The Sodi network was one of the first long-tail investigations at the Zondo Commission of Inquiry into State Capture, which revealed sub-national or provincial capture when Ace Magashule was Free State premier.

Now in jail facing attempted murder as well as fraud and corruption charges, Matlala is also down on his luck.

![Naledi-Caryn-SAPS](https://cdn.dailymaverick.co.za/i/g2XyV-GiOjtKMxdx7dCh3G-itFI=/200x100/smart/filters:strip_exif()/file/attachments/orphans/6I1A7412_689643.jpg "Vusimuzi Matlala, charged on 24 March 2026, along with senior SAPS officers, including generals and high-ranking officials linked to supply chain management, over alleged involvement in a R360m corruption scandal. The accused appeared before the Pretoria Magistrates' Court on 25 March 2026. (Photo: Felix Dlangamandla)")

Vusimuzi Matlala, charged on 24 March 2026, along with senior SAPS officers, including generals and high-ranking officials linked to supply chain management, over alleged involvement in a R360m corruption scandal. The accused appeared before the Pretoria Magistrates' Court on 25 March 2026. (Photo: Felix Dlangamandla)

This week, Nkosi linked Matlala to Mashatile, a claim the deputy president’s spokesperson Khoza quickly refuted, as [Vincent Cruywagen reported]( on 24 March 2026 ) in Daily Maverick.

But note how close and comfortable Khoza looked at the table. We asked him about the image and whether Mashatile had ever met Matlala.

“The DP \[deputy president\] does not know Mr Matlala and has never had contact with him. With regards to me, I don’t know him at all. We happened to be at the same party where there were many people I did not know, including him. I only saw this picture when the media showed it. At the party, I never interacted with him or sat with him. Even in the picture, I was talking to Edwin, not him,” said Khoza.

What the image confirms is how tender kingpins like Sodi, the Guptas, the Bosasa network of the Watson family and [Angelo Aggrizzi](https://www.dailymaverick.co.za/article/2025-11-06-national-prosecuting-authority-defends-plea-deal-that-allows-agrizzi-to-walk-free/), and now Matlala, cultivate political sponsors through giving them access to a lifestyle they cannot afford. Mashatile enjoyed lux holidays at Sodi’s beachfront properties before the tender kingpin hit the skids.

At the table were other politicians, as News24 reported.

### Anatomy of patronage

The Madlanga Commission has also shown how Matlala had already conquered the sub-national state and the ANC in particular. In North West, he had the ANC influencer Brown Mogotsi on his payroll.

The first tranche of testimony in the cross-examination of local party man Suleiman Carrim revealed [money flows](https://www.dailymaverick.co.za/article/2026-03-09-tenders-tycoons-and-threats-suleiman-cacarrims-day-of-reckoning-at-the-madlanga/) between him and Matlala, which the commission heard may involve money-laundering.

Matlala allegedly paid former police minister Bheki Cele in cash, and the former police minister also stayed at his luxury Menlyn penthouse apartment, testimony has [revealed](https://www.dailymaverick.co.za/article/2025-11-26-cele-lied-vusimuzi-cat-matlala-alleges-es-he-made-r500k-payoff-to-former-police/).

It’s a well-worn pattern, and Matlala was on his way up into the highest political ranks until investigative reports by News24 and Mkhwanazi’s [bombshell](https://www.dailymaverick.co.za/article/2025-07-07-mkhwanazis-warning-drug-cartel-criminal-syndicate-infest-sa-law-enforcement/) gave the country a wake-up. The commission and parliamentary inquiry followed.

In patronage network theory, there is usually a controller who cultivates political elites to win contracts for rent extraction from the state. In the book, Shadow State, the Politics of State Capture, edited by Ivor Chipkin and Mark Swilling, the anatomy of a patronage network shows this structure.

Matlala was developing a capture network and aiming for national figures until he was stopped in his tracks. The commission, as well as the arrest of 12 figures in Matlala’s network, most of them in the police, show that what was under way was a deepening of capture.

![Fer-Cat-Paul](https://cdn.dailymaverick.co.za/i/QTyb32WNL4RZRwvoxsUvSHFbGKw=/200x100/smart/filters:strip_exif()/file/attachments/orphans/Summary-of-the-Main-Accused_720203.jpg)

Fer-Cat-Paul

![Fer-Cat-Paul](https://cdn.dailymaverick.co.za/i/1cI2ljC85zsjhfwNXqEdBGMyYOA=/200x100/smart/filters:strip_exif()/file/attachments/orphans/Simplified-Summary-of-the-Case_755502.jpg)

Fer-Cat-Paul

After the entrenchment of patronage networks and State Capture, the next step is the criminalisation of the state, where crime networks infiltrate and take over key parts of the state. Consider it a kind of Gupta 2.0 of capture.

South Africa has come close, the Madlanga Commission is revealing. The big question is whether such infiltration has been disrupted. **DM**

_We thank News24 for granting permission for the use of the image._

9 LIVES | How the 'Cat' captured the heart of the SAPS

[Skip to main content](#article)

![](./assets/mhFuHZzi2d/brand-logos-news24-trustednews.svg)![](./assets/mhFuHZzi2d/brand-logos-news24-trustednews.svg)

  ![](./assets/ttmdVf5u8X/9-lives-shorthand.gif) 

**Jeff Wicks – News24 Investigations**

News24's investigation spanned months and exposed how tenderpreneur **Vusimusi "Cat" Matlala** steered a web of control that reached the highest echelons of South African policing.

After securing a R360-million SAPS health services tender, despite zero qualifications, amid allegations of fraud, fronting and collusion, Matlala's influence extended to **Police Minister Senzo Mchunu** and former **minister Bheki Cele.**

Our 9 LIVES investigation revealed how Matlala – previously flagged by murdered whistleblower Babita Deokaran for suspicious Tembisa Hospital contracts – funded an extravagant lifestyle of Rolls-Royces, designer clothing, and mansions, while his company, Medicare24, failed to deliver services and left employees unpaid.

This multilayered investigation traced the deadly intersection of **tender fraud, political protection, and criminal violence** – showing how R50 million in taxpayer money disappeared while officials looked away.

# **Prince of Pretoria: Cat Matlala posed as Eswatini royal to secure R95k-a-month mansion**

Tenderpreneur and fraud accused Vusimusi “Cat” Matlala allegedly posed as an Eswatini prince to secure a lease for a luxury, multimillion-rand Pretoria mansion.

[Read the article here](https://www.news24.com/investigations/prince-of-pretoria-cat-matlala-posed-as-eswatini-royal-to-secure-r95k-a-month-mansion-20260418-1060)

 

 

# **WATCH | The moneyman: How Cat Matlala’s Mike van Wyk charmed EMPD’s Mkhwanazi**

Vusimusi “Cat” Matlala infiltrated the South African Police Service and the Ekurhuleni Metro Police Department (EMPD) through the connivance of senior officers and the influence of his allies.

[WATCH the video here](https://www.news24.com/investigations/watch-money-mike-van-wyk-cat-matlalas-silent-influencer-peddler-20260329-1034)

 

   

# **Why national police commissioner Fannie Masemola will face charges tied to Cat Matlala**

National police commissioner Fannie Masemola is staring down criminal prosecution related to Vusimusi “Cat” Matlala’s sullied police tender and payments worth R50 million after he was warned, twice, of potential fraud.

[Read the article here](https://www.news24.com/investigations/why-national-police-commissioner-fannie-masemola-will-face-charges-tied-to-cat-matlala-20260325-1201)

 

 

# **Inside top cop arrest blitz over Cat Matlala's tainted R360m police tender**

Vusimusi “Cat” Matlala and 12 high-ranking police officers face fraud and corruption charges over a R360-million police health tender scandal. The officers allegedly helped the notorious tenderpreneur illegally secure the lucrative contract through systematic bid-rigging.

[Read the article here](https://www.news24.com/investigations/12-top-cops-cuffed-over-cat-matlalas-rigged-r360m-police-tender-20260324-1085)

Vusimusi “Cat” Matlala lavished a high-ranking cop with gifts of cash and Ozempic – his largesse buying him access to an official in the police’s back-office management.

[Read the article here](https://www.news24.com/investigations/cat-matlala-the-ozempic-diva-cop-and-his-secret-saps-deepthroat-20260205-0510)

 

   

# **From grill to gold: How Cat Matlala’s wife scored R3.7m Ekurhuleni deal**

Tsakane Matlala, Vusimusi “Cat” Matlala’s wife, scored a R3.7-million Ekurhuleni Metropolitan Municipality contract using a company she had controlled for just 10 days.

[Read the article here](https://www.news24.com/investigations/from-grill-to-gold-how-cat-matlalas-wife-scored-r37m-ekurhuleni-deal-20260201-1051)

 

   

# **High flying: How Cat Matlala courted Nedbank for lux R70m OR Tambo terminal deal**

Vusimusi “Cat” Matlala planned to build a luxury private terminal at OR Tambo International Airport and was in talks with Nedbank for R70 million per year in funding.

[Read the article here](https://www.news24.com/investigations/high-flying-how-cat-matlala-courted-nedbank-for-lux-r70m-or-tambo-terminal-deal-20260114-1077)

Vusimusi “Cat” Matlala lied to Parliament’s ad hoc committee when he told MPs his vehicles were not fitted with blue lights, shifting blame for the use of these lights to his estranged ex-wife.

[Read the article here](https://www.news24.com/investigations/same-car-new-wife-cat-matlalas-blue-light-lies-unravel-with-new-sun-city-holiday-video-20251128-1017)

 

   

# **Tender prophet Cat Matlala rented SAPS medical clinic 6 months before R360m award**

Vusimusi Cat Matlala rented a clinic on South African Police Service (SAPS) property six months before he scored a tainted R360 million police health services tender.

[Read the article here](https://www.news24.com/investigations/tender-prophet-cat-matlala-rented-saps-medical-clinic-6-months-before-r360m-award-20251109-1235)

 

   

# **Cat Matlala’s tender kickback cops and secret cash scheme exposed**

Vusimusi “Cat” Matlala channelled cash to high-ranking cops after he landed a R360-million police health services tender. News24 can reveal that the tenderpreneur made payments seemingly intended for Brigadier Rachel Matjeng, in the police’s finance section, and Captain Brian Cartwright. 

[Read the article here](https://www.news24.com/investigations/cat-matlalas-tender-kickback-cops-and-secret-cash-scheme-exposed-20250914-0903)

 

   

# **Cele, Matlala held secret summit at Tembisa tender don’s Zimbali villa**

Former Police Minister Bheki Cele held a secret meeting with Cat Matlala at Ballito’s plush Zimbali estate, in a villa owned by Tembisa Hospital tender don, Morgan Maumela.

[Read the article here](https://www.news24.com/investigations/cele-matlala-held-secret-summit-at-tembisa-tender-dons-zimbali-villa-20250910-1252)

 

   

# **10 missed calls: Bheki Cele’s frantic efforts to talk to tender kingpin ‘Cat’ Matlala**

Tender don Vusimusi “Cat” Matlala built a life of wealth from state tenders, both at Tembisa Hospital and the SAPS, and has been accused of capturing politicians. Bheki Cele denies the pair are friends. Extensive contact by phone tells a conflicting story.

[Read the article here](https://www.news24.com/investigations/10-missed-calls-bheki-celes-frantic-efforts-to-talk-to-tender-kingpin-cat-matlala-20250824-1085)

 

   

### **‘Cat’ Matlala to face charges for botched hits on taxi boss ‘Joe Ferrari’, DJ Vettys**

Tender don Vusimusi “Cat” Matlala will face charges for botched hits targeting taxi boss Joe Sibanyoni and DJ Vettys, with ballistic analysis linking seized guns to at least 10 high-profile killings.

[Read the article here](https://www.news24.com/investigations/9-lives-cat-matlala-to-face-charges-for-botched-hits-on-taxi-boss-joe-ferrari-dj-vettys-20250724-1200)

 

   

### **How Cat Matlala bankrolled Crime Intelligence cop’s glitzy ANC gala jamboree**

Vusimusi “Cat” Matlala sponsored a high-ranking Crime Intelligence cop, Colonel Smanga Simelane, and five others on a jaunt to the ANC’s January 8 celebrations in Cape Town earlier this year. 

[Read the article here](https://www.news24.com/investigations/9-lives-how-cat-matlala-bankrolled-crime-intelligence-cops-glitzy-anc-gala-jamboree-20250709-1171)

 

   

### **Bheki Cele stayed at police tender tycoon Matlala’s luxury penthouse**

Vusimusi “Cat” Matlala lavished former police minister Bheki Cele with stays in an exclusive penthouse in a Pretoria hotel.

[Read the article here](https://www.news24.com/investigations/9-lives-bheki-cele-stayed-at-police-tender-tycoon-matlalas-luxury-penthouse-20250707-1151)

 

   

### **Tender King ‘Cat’ Matlala and Senzo Mchunu linked to protection bribe scandal**

KwaZulu-Natal police commissioner Nhlanhla Mkhwanazi publicly declared that the SAPS has been infiltrated by underworld syndicates that control key cops. He accused Police Minister Senzo Mchunu of disbanding the police’s political killings task team for ulterior motives. Tender kingpin Vusimusi ‘Cat’ Matlala is at the centre of it all.

[Read the article here](https://www.news24.com/investigations/9-lives-tender-king-cat-matlala-and-senzo-mchunu-linked-in-protection-bribe-scandal-20250706-0952)

 

   

### **How Vusimusi ‘Cat’ Matlala clawed in R50m from SAPS despite corruption red flags**

Police top brass paid Vusimusi “Cat” Matlala R30 million – on top of R18 million already disbursed – after they were warned that his company’s tainted R360 million health services tender was beset by claims of fronting, collusion and fraud.

[Read the article here](https://www.news24.com/investigations/9-lives-how-vusimusi-cat-matlala-clawed-in-r50m-from-saps-despite-corruption-red-flags-20250701-1156)

 

   

### **Crime, killers, and contracts: The dark past of tender king Cat Matlala unravelled**

Tender don Vusimusi Cat Matlala has a past straddling the criminal underworld and was once arrested with crime boss Radovan Krecjir’s most feared hitmen.

[Read the article here](https://www.news24.com/investigations/9-lives-crime-killers-and-contracts-the-dark-past-of-tender-king-cat-matlala-unravelled-20250529-1109)

 

   

### **A Rolls-Royce, mansions and cosmetic surgery - Cat Matlala’s R360m tender splurge**

While controversial tenderpreneur Vusimusi Cat Matlala lavished his family with expensive clothing, cosmetic surgery, and mansion life, his staff and subcontractors were hit hard in a wave of bad debt he left after his R360 million police tender was scotched.

[Read the article here](https://www.news24.com/investigations/9-lives-from-rolls-royce-to-ruin-inside-cat-matlalas-tender-life-of-excess-20250528-1136)

 

   

### **Cat Matlala’s R360m police deal cancelled days before criminal probe begins**

National police commissioner Fannie Masemola has cancelled a R360-million tender awarded to Vusimusi Cat Matlala as allegations of fraud, collusion and flouting of procurement law - which first surfaced three months ago - continue to mount.

[Read the article here](https://www.news24.com/investigations/9-lives-cat-matlalas-r360m-police-deal-cancelled-days-before-criminal-probe-begins-20250518-1193)

 

   

### **Tender king Cat Matlala arrested for botched hit on socialite ex-lover** 

Vusimusi Cat Matlala is a tenderpreneur who made his fortune through state contracts, and last year scored a R360 million deal from the police. On Wednesday, he was arrested and charged for allegedly masterminding a murder.

[Read the article here](https://www.news24.com/investigations/9-lives-tender-king-cat-matlala-arrested-for-botched-hit-on-socialite-ex-lover-20250514-1159)

 

   

### **Tender tycoon Cat Matlala is person of interest in Tebogo Thobejane attempted hit**

Tenderpreneur Vusimusi "Cat" Matlala is a person of interest in a police investigation centred on the botched murder of socialite, influencer and actress Tebogo Thobejane in 2023. This is the latest scandal to blight his R360-million tender windfall, awarded by the same organisation investigating him for conspiracy and attempted murder. He has denied wrongdoing.

[Read the article here](https://www.news24.com/investigations/9-lives-tender-tycoon-cat-matlala-is-person-of-interest-in-tebogo-thobejane-attempted-hit-20250503)

 

   

### **National police commissioner ignored fraud warnings in R360m SAPS tender scandal**

The award of a R360-million SAPS tender to state-procurement doyen Vusimusi Cat Matlala was riven by irregularities, misrepresentation and scandal, according to an internal audit. Top cop Fannie Masemola was warned about this in January and advised to cancel the tender. He didn't.

[Read the article here](https://www.news24.com/investigations/9-lives-national-police-commissioner-ignored-fraud-warnings-in-r360m-saps-tender-scandal-20250422)

 

   

### **Tender 'Cat' risks losing R360m police deal in fronting, fraud scandal**

Police commissioner Fannie Masemola has threatened to cancel a controversial R360-million health services tender - clinched by tender baron Vusimusi Cat Matlala - amid allegations of fronting, fraud and a failure to deliver.

[Read the article here](https://www.news24.com/investigations/9-lives-tender-cat-risks-losing-r360m-police-deal-in-fronting-fraud-scandal-20250329)

 

   

### **Tender tycoon Cat Matlala faces liquidation as R360m police contract hits the skids**

Tender tycoon Vusimusi Cat Matlala, who scored a R360 million police health services deal, cannot deliver on the tender and faces liquidation while struggling to pay his staff and suppliers.

[Read the article here](https://www.news24.com/investigations/9-lives-tender-tycoon-cat-matlala-faces-liquidation-as-r360m-police-contract-hits-the-skids-20250328)

 

   

### **Ex-top cop helped approve R360m tender - now she works for Tembisa tycoon who scored deal**

A little-known company controlled by Tembisa Hospital tycoon Vusimusi Cat Matlala landed a R360-million police tender midway through 2024. A high-ranking cop on the panel, who appointed Matlala’s firm, resigned three weeks before the deal was awarded and now works with the man she helped appoint.

[Read the article here](https://www.news24.com/investigations/9-lives-ex-top-cop-helped-approve-r360m-tender-now-she-works-fortembisa-tycoon-who-scored-deal-20250314)

 

   

### **How tender magnate handed R360m police deal to placeholder director**

Tembisa Hospital tycoon Vusimusi 'Cat' Matlala resigned his directorship in a company six months after it landed a R360 million police health services tender, handing control to a 29-year-old woman with no business background.

[Read the article here](https://www.news24.com/investigations/paris-paper-queen-how-tender-magnate-handed-r360m-police-deal-to-placeholder-director-20250305)

# Top Saps General Denies “Cat” Matlala Funding Claims Amid Corruption Probe

[Participate in Parliament](https://www.parliament.gov.za/participate-parliament) » News Details

![](/storage/app/media/1_Stock/Police/SAPS_badge_large.jpg)

The Ad Hoc Committee established to investigate allegations relating to the South African Police Service (SAPS) heard testimony from Lieutenant General (Lt Gen) Hilda Senthumule denying that businessman Mr Vusimuzi “Cat” Matlala ever paid for her cosmetic surgery.

She faced questions about alleged crime kingpin Mr Matlala’s donations to the SAPS National Excellence Awards, and claims relating to payment from Mr Matlala for plastic surgery known as a Brazilian butt lift and for weight-loss injections.

During the proceedings, she stood up and twirled before the committee when the matter of the plastic surgery arose during questioning, indicating that she did not have such a procedure done. She explained, while also attaching bank statements as evidence, that she had a liposuction operation, but she had paid for it out of her own pocket.

During her testimony this month she also addressed a range of other issues concerning police governance and the removal of dockets.

 Lt Gen Senthumule’s appearance forms part of the committee’s ongoing inquiry into serious allegations of corruption and interference within SAPS. During her testimony, she outlined her professional responsibilities and responded to questions from committee members regarding decision-making processes and internal lines of accountability.

A significant portion of the engagement focused on allegations raised before the committee concerning Lt Gen Senthumule’s alleged relationship with Mr Matlala. Members questioned her about claims that he may have had undue influence and that he allegedly funded personal expenses, including the cosmetic procedure.

Lt Gen Senthumule addressed these claims during the session, responding to Members’ questions and disputing aspects of the allegations. She emphasised her commitment to ethical conduct and denied any improper relationship that would compromise her duties as a senior police official.

Committee members stressed the seriousness of the allegations, noting that any suggestion of undue influence or personal benefit linked to external individuals would represent a significant breach of public trust. They underscored the need for full transparency and indicated that all claims must be thoroughly tested through evidence.

In addition, Members engaged with Lt Gen Senthumule on broader institutional challenges, including coordination gaps, internal communication failures, and the handling of sensitive information within SAPS. Concerns were also raised about delays in addressing critical issues and the need for stronger consequence management mechanisms.

The committee reiterated its commitment to a fair, evidence-based inquiry aimed at strengthening oversight and restoring confidence in SAPS. Proceedings are expected to continue in the coming weeks as further witnesses are called to testify.

**Rajaa Azzakani**  
**30 March 2026**

# Mkhwanazi Inquiry: Mr Vusimuzi Matlala

#### [Ad Hoc Committee to Investigate Allegations made by Lieutenant General Nhlanhla Mkhwanazi](/committee/391/)

##### 27 November 2025

##### Chairperson: Mr S Lekganyane (ANC)

Share this page:

### Meeting Summary

[Video](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=nJG6hIf_ZsY)

[Ad Hoc Committee on Gen Mkhwanazi's Allegations](https://www.parliament.gov.za/ad-hoc-committee-gen-mkhwanazis-allegations)

The Committee’s second day engagement with Mr Vusimuzi Matlala focused on clarifying his role in several controversial financial and interpersonal interactions involving senior officials in the South African Police Service and individuals claiming political connections. Members of the Committee sought to determine whether his conduct amounted to inappropriate influence, corrupt activity, or participation in networks that undermine accountability within law-enforcement structures.

A significant area of investigation was his relationship with Mr Brown Mogotsi, who had presented himself as someone with access to high-level political offices. Mr Matlala stated that he did not verify Mogotsi’s identity or the claims he made, even though he repeatedly gave him large sums of money. Committee members criticised this lack of due diligence, particularly because the transactions were frequent and involved substantial amounts. They also questioned his explanation that he initially refused to fund political activities but later financed transport and accommodation for individuals travelling to the African National Congress January 8th event. These inconsistencies raised concerns about whether he was more deeply involved in political activities than he admitted.

Much of the meeting focused on his interactions with former Minister of Police, Mr Bheki Cele. The Committee probed his account that he sought assistance from Cele to recover firearms that the South African Police Service had seized and that Cele later made ongoing financial demands. Members pressed him on why he continued meeting these demands if he felt the requests had become unreasonable. They argued that this pattern resembled an exchange of favours that blurred ethical boundaries and created opportunities for undue influence.

The Committee also questioned his meeting with Lieutenant-General Nhlanhla Mkhwanazi. This meeting, arranged through Cele, was intended to address delays in payments owed to Mr Matlala’s businesses by the South African Police Service. Members challenged the appropriateness of approaching such a senior official outside formal procurement and administrative processes. They noted that this created the impression of privileged access and the potential for interference in operational matters. They explored whether the engagement was intended to influence investigations or secure preferential treatment within procurement systems. Mr Matlala denied offering anything of value to Lieutenant-General Mkhwanazi but admitted that the General raised a personal issue about the withdrawal of a torture allegation made by another individual.

Further scrutiny was directed at the WhatsApp messages included in the annexures to his statement. Members asked why some messages appeared to originate from profiles saved under different names and why certain exchanges suggested involvement in matters beyond his stated role. While he claimed some messages may have been altered, Members were not convinced, given that the data was extracted directly from his phone. He also stated that he could not re-access the messages due to technical issues.

Questions regarding his financial capacity and lifestyle were also raised. Members asked him to account for multiple properties, frequent travel, the use of bodyguards and the costs associated with supporting a large household. They doubted whether his declared business interests could sustain such expenses and noted that aspects of his financial affairs were under investigation by the Special Investigating Unit. He insisted that all his income was legitimate and traceable.

Throughout the meeting, the Committee highlighted contradictions in his testimony and gaps in his explanations. Members emphasised that the interactions he described pointed to systemic vulnerabilities within the South African Police Service, including the influence of informal networks, unverified intermediaries and blurred boundaries between business interests and policing functions.

### Meeting report

Chairperson: Good morning. The Senior Counsel (SC) will have two hours to conclude his leading of the evidence. Thereafter, Members will be given an opportunity to ask questions.

Adv Norman Arendse, SC, Evidence Leader: Good morning, Mr Matlala.

Mr Vusimuzi “Cat” Matlala (Witness): Good morning.

Adv Arendse: Mr Matlala, I just want to kick off with your allegations regarding former Minister Cele. You made some allegations yesterday which are clearly very serious, that you made two payments to him. You dealt with that in your statement at page26 and 27. Do you still have a copy of your revised statement?

Mr Matlala: Yes, I do.

Adv Arendse: That is where you deal with the payments. An initial payment was made at your residence around January. Do you have a more or less exact date in January that you made this payment?

Mr Matlala: No, I do not.

Adv Arendse: And you said you handed the money to him while you were in your apartment?

Mr Matlala: Yes.

Adv Arendse: Were the two of you alone?

Mr Matlala: No, I said we were with Mr Bongani Mpungose.

Adv Arendse: So Bongani Mpungose would have witnessed you making the payment?

Mr Matlala: Yeah, but unfortunately he passed on.

Adv Arendse: He passed on? You do not have a live witness?

Mr Matlala: No, I do not have.

Adv Arendse: How did you get this money? Did you go and withdraw it at the bank or at an ATM? And you would have a bank account. Can you produce your bank statements to show a withdrawal of a cash amount either at the ATM or at the bank?

Mr Matlala: Yes, I do not have access to my banking app, but the police do have a copy of my bank statement. I cannot get bank statements from here.

Adv Arendse: So we can at some point get a copy of your bank statement?

Mr Matlala: Yes, I think if I can check, because I already have the disclosure of the docket from a criminal case, chances are the statement might be there as well.

Adv Arendse: Okay. We will see if we cannot get access to that bank statement. So just tell us what the circumstances were. Did he ask to stay at your apartment, or did you offer that he stay at your apartment?

Mr Matlala: Yes, he asked.

Adv Arendse: What was his reason? When he testified before this Committee, he \[said\] he is a pensioner, and if there is an offer by someone to stay in their apartment, he is not going to say no, and it sounds quite plausible. But now you say he asked to stay at your apartment. So at what point does he ask you for money, or do you offer him money? And what amount?

Mr Matlala: The first payment was R300 000. It was in January this year. The reason for me to give him that money is because he asked for money.

Adv Arendse: He asked for the money?

Mr Matlala: Yes.

Adv Arendse: Did he mention R300 000?

Mr Matlala: No, he actually wanted R1 million.

Adv Arendse: Your response was ‘I cannot give you R1 million, but I can give you R300 000’?

Mr Matlala: No, I did not \[only\] give him R300 000. I gave him R3\[00 000\], and then I gave him R2\[00 000\], like I mentioned. The day I decided to stop I was supposed to give him R300 000, but that never happened. It is when I decided to stop taking his calls.

Adv Arendse: So just to summarise, he wanted R1 million?

Mr Matlala: Yes.

Adv Arendse: And you made two payments to him of R500 000?

Mr Matlala: Yes.

Adv Arendse: And when the balance was demanded, you stopped?

Mr Matlala: Yes.

Adv Arendse: Let us go to the first occasion. When did he make his demand for R1 million? Was it before he came to stay at your apartment? Was it at your apartment or in your apartment?

Mr Matlala: Yes, at my apartment.

Adv Arendse: And you say that at the time the late Mpungose was present?

Mr Matlala: Yes.

Adv Arendse: And what was your reaction to someone of that stature demanding R1 million from you?

Mr Matlala: He actually spoke to Bongani. He said ‘You see, I helped your friend, and now I am here at his apartment, and he is not even doing anything to show appreciation.’ And then I said, ‘but what do you mean, because I even offered you a place to stay?’ He said, ‘No, but this will not pay my bills, so you know that I have helped you, but in return you are not doing anything.’ That is when I said ‘Okay, how much do you want me to give you?’ And then he said to me that ‘If you can give me R1 million’ he would appreciate that.

Adv Arendse: Why did you not mention that in your statement?

Mr Matlala: Mention what?

Adv Arendse: In your statement, you did not mention that he demanded R1 million from you, and that you made only part payment to him of R300 \[000\] and then R200 \[000\].

Mr Matlala: There is actually a lot of things that I did not mention. Like I said to you, I forgot a lot of things. The place that I am in, I cannot remember all these things. Some of them, like I said yesterday, that I just remember when I am lying in bed. I am being locked in a cell for 23 hours a day, so I have no contact. I do not have \[a\] radio. I do not have \[a\] newspaper. I do not have \[a\] TV. I am blocked from the outside world, so my brain is not functioning well. For that, please forgive me.

Adv Arendse: But you would agree that this is a very significant event? One, it involves a former Minister – General Cele. Two, it involves you. You are now in the midst of having to almost fight for your life. You have been raided twice by the Political Killings Task Team (PKTT). You are a sought-after person. You are in the midst of tendering for a huge award, R350 million. Why would you not remember or recall some of these significant events?

Mr Matlala: You are saying why would I not remember what?

Adv Arendse: Why would you not have recalled that his demand was actually for a million Rand?

Mr Matlala: I do not have control of my memory. What my memory decides to forget, I do not have control over that. So I just remembered it.

Adv Arendse: Okay. So all this is said initially in your apartment?

Mr Matlala: Yes.

Adv Arendse: So when he asked to stay at your apartment, you were comfortable with the fact that, well, he did you a favour; the alleged harassment of the police had stopped. Your firearms have been returned. And you are quite okay to give him access to your apartment. So up until that point, everything is fine with you?

Mr Matlala: Before the money part?

Adv Arendse: Yeah, before the money part.

Mr Matlala: Yes, I did not have a problem with that.

Adv Arendse: Why did you not tell him ‘I am sorry \[but\] I am not going to give you any money. You have done me a favour. Thank you very much. I am doing you a favour by allowing you to stay in my apartment free of charge. Why must I pay you more money?’

Mr Matlala: I do not think if you were in my shoes, you would do the same because I have witnessed what these people were doing to me. And then I know this person, so I would not want to provoke him or say something that I know he would not like.

Adv Arendse: Okay. So when he mentioned the money, what did you say? How did that conversation go?

Mr Matlala: Yes, I said for now what I can arrange is R300 000 because I had other things to do with money. He accepted it.

Adv Arendse: You have that kind of money in your bank account?

Mr Matlala: Yes.

Adv Arendse: How much money did you have in your bank account at that time?

Mr Matlala: I do not remember.

Adv Arendse: Is that your personal bank account or business bank account?

Mr Matlala: It is a business \[account\].

Adv Arendse: And which of the five businesses?

Mr Matlala: It is \[the\] Medicare24 business account.

Adv Arendse: And you say that a bank statement of that account has already been obtained by the police?

Mr Matlala: I believe so.

Adv Arendse: And that you will make it available to us?

Mr Matlala: I am not promising. I will have to check with my legal team. What I know is they have pulled bank statements of all my accounts, but I am hoping even the Medicare\[24\] one should be there.

Adv Arendse: So what will those bank accounts show?

Mr Matlala: The withdrawal from the bank.

Adv Arendse: They will show a withdrawal of cash?

Mr Matlala: Yes.

Adv Arendse: At the bank?

Mr Matlala: Yes.

Adv Arendse: Which bank? Which branch?

Mr Matlala: Menlyn Maine.

Adv Arendse: Which bank?

Mr Matlala: First National Bank (FNB).

Adv Arendse: And you went in as an ordinary client or customer to the bank, and you said to them, ‘I would like to withdraw R300 000?’

Mr Matlala: By that time (in December), I resigned as a director. So my sister was the director (in January). So I sent her to withdraw the money on my behalf.

Adv Arendse: What is her name again?

Mr Matlala: Claudette.

Adv Arendse: Surname?

Mr Matlala: Masethe.

Adv Arendse: Okay. So she actually went to withdraw the money?

Mr Matlala: Yes.

Adv Arendse: Because you did not have the authority to withdraw that kind of money from the company's bank account?

Mr Matlala: She is the account holder now because she was the director.

Adv Arendse: So you make these arrangements with her while you are in your apartment? Did you text her? Did you phone her?

Mr Matlala: I do not remember. I think I called or texted.

Adv Arendse: You tell her ‘I need R300 000 in cash’?

Mr Matlala: Yes.

Adv Arendse: She goes and draws the money?

Mr Matlala: Yes.

Adv Arendse: And how long did this take place, this whole transaction, from the time that you called her or messaged her, and she goes to the bank and comes back to the apartment?

Mr Matlala: If you order it today, by tomorrow you can go and withdraw the money. But sometimes if they do have money in the branch, you can get it the same day.

Adv Arendse: So did they have money that day at the branch?

Mr Matlala: I do not remember whether it was the same day or we went the following day.

Adv Arendse: So what are you now saying, that the handing over of the cash of R300 000 to former Minister Cele, did not take place on the same day or the first day that he stayed in your apartment?

Mr Matlala: Yes, I do not remember the exact day, whether it is the first day when he came or the following day.

Adv Arendse: Well, at least you can remember that, whether it was the same day or the next day.

Mr Matlala: No, I do not remember.

Adv Arendse: You cannot remember?

Mr Matlala: No, I cannot.

Adv Arendse: You also testified that the late Mpungose was the one who was present when General Cele made this demand?

Mr Matlala: Yes.

Adv Arendse: But when the money was actually handed over, was he also present?

Mr Matlala: Yes.

Adv Arendse: Why would he have been present? Is he also staying in your apartment? Or did you arrange to have him present so that you could have a witness?

Mr Matlala: Mr Vele was closer to him than me. Mr Mpungose is the one who arranged \[for\] me to go and meet him in the first place. So every morning when he was in my apartment, he would drive and go and sit with him there. If I am not doing anything, I would come and join them sometimes. Sometimes I would leave both of them there together and go do whatever I needed to do.

Adv Arendse: So is it the case that the late Mr Mpungose was a kind of a chaperone to former General Cele? Was he kind of a companion to him?

Mr Matlala: Yeah, he was, because at some point I remember they borrowed my car to drop him off at the airport. So most of the times he was with him.

Adv Arendse: So, just come back to the cash. So your colleague, the director of the company now, how was this money transported and brought to your apartment?

Mr Matlala: We walked.

Adv Arendse: You walked?

Mr Matlala: Yes.

Adv Arendse: From your apartment to the bank?

Mr Matlala: Yes.

Adv Arendse: So is it within walking distance?

Mr Matlala: Yes.

Adv Arendse: Did she walk?

Mr Matlala: Yes. I walked to the apartment with the money.

Adv Arendse: So you went to your apartment with the money?

Mr Matlala: Yes.

Adv Arendse: After picking up the money from her, were you at the bank or some other place?

Mr Matlala: Yes, in the bank.

Adv Arendse: Were you accompanied from the bank to your apartment with such a huge amount of money?

Mr Matlala: No, I was not accompanied. I do not know if you know Menlyn Maine? You can actually walk from inside the mall. You do not need to get outside the mall and go to my apartment. So you can just walk right inside and go upstairs with the elevator to the penthouse.

Adv Arendse: Did you walk alone?

Mr Matlala: I am saying from the bank, I was with my sister, and then she went to her place, and then I went to the apartment.

Adv Arendse: And I know you have your own personal VIP protection services company, but that was a huge amount of money to walk with. Was it in a bag, in a suitcase? In a Woollies bag? How did you move that kind of money?

Mr Matlala: Yes, it was inside the Woollies shopping bag.

Adv Arendse: So they have other uses?

Mr Matlala: Yes, they do.

Adv Arendse: Okay. And in the meantime, Minister Cele is in the apartment with Mpungose waiting for you to bring the money?

Mr Matlala: Yes.

Adv Arendse: That was the first occasion. Do you know how Minister Cele would have travelled from Durban to Pretoria? Was it by road? Did he fly?

Mr Matlala: I think he would fly most of the times.

Adv Arendse: You mentioned that Mpungose used…

Mr Matlala: I borrowed him a car once.

Adv Arendse: To the airport. Now, for someone to travel, whether it is by road or air, with R300 000 in a Woollies bag, that sounds really far-fetched.

Mr Matlala: How?

Adv Arendse: Well, I would not travel with R5000, knowing that you are at risk of – if you are on the road – being hijacked, being stopped, or just misplacing the money.

Mr Matlala: I do not believe so.

Adv Arendse: All I am putting to you is it is a highly unusual situation that you give R300 000 to a person in a Woollies bag, and that person presumably took it back home to where he stays in KwaZulu-Natal (KZN).

Mr Matlala: I did not say he took it back to KZN. I do not know where he took the money to. I just gave him the money. What did he do with the money? I do not know.

Adv Arendse: Well, he obviously took the money. It was not any longer in your apartment.

Mr Matlala: Yes.

Adv Arendse: How long did he stay at your apartment?

Mr Matlala: I think he came to visit three or four times. I do not remember well. Sometimes for three days, four days, two days.

Adv Arendse: After the first transaction of R300 000, you cannot remember how many days he stayed at your apartment?

Mr Matlala: I was not keeping count.

Adv Arendse: When you made the second payment to him of R200 000, which you say was around about March 2025, that was at the Beverly Hills Hotel?

Mr Matlala: Yes, that is correct.

Adv Arendse: How did that happen? Was it in your hotel room or did you arrange a room?

Mr Matlala: No, we were having lunch outside by the patio. That day I was with my protectors. And then me and him, we walked outside the hotel. There is parking outside the hotel. And then I asked one of my protectors to go to my car and give me the bag. And then I took that bag. I went with him to his car. I remember he was driving a red Jeep. I gave him, then he put the money inside the Jeep and then he drove off.

Adv Arendse: And you say that was his red Jeep?

Mr Matlala: I am saying he was driving a red Jeep. Whether it is his or not, I do not know.

Adv Arendse: And there at the Beverly Hills, is it that he asked you again for the balance or asked you specifically for R200 000? How did that happen?

Mr Matlala: He would not say a specific amount. He would just call and say, ‘Do something.’ Whether it is R300 \[000\], R500 \[000\], R 200 \[000\], whatever I had at that time. Then I would just go and drop it off.

Adv Arendse: This happened in March? This is now some two months or so after the first transaction, is that right?

Mr Matlala: Yes.

Adv Arendse: And did you have any communication with him in between that period, phone calls, WhatsApps?

Mr Matlala: Yes, we had. Not WhatsApps. Phone calls.

Adv Arendse: One should be able to see from your telephone records whether there was some call? Obviously, it would not be recorded.

Mr Matlala: I do not know if you can get \[it\], but my phone is here. It can be taken to the forensic and they can check. Even his missed calls are still there.

Adv Arendse: If I remember correctly, General Cele said he does not even send WhatsApps to his wife.

Mr Matlala: Not WhatsApps.

Adv Arendse: I can understand perhaps it was not a WhatsApp, but you say it would have been a phone call.

Mr Matlala: It is still WhatsApp, but a WhatsApp call.

Adv Arendse: That was the second occasion, in March. And by now you would have been aware that there has been a directive that's been issued by Minister Mchunu to disband the PKTT? You were aware of that by March?

Mr Matlala: Yes, I was aware.

Adv Arendse: Even in January?

Mr Matlala: Yes.

Adv Arendse: We are going to deal with that. What was the purpose of your meeting with former Minister Cele in March at the Beverly Hills Hotel?

Mr Matlala: It was about me giving him that money. And then obviously when I get there we talk about other things. I remember I was talking to him about \[the\] South African Police Services (SAPS) not giving me work anymore, \[and\] my payments being delayed from SAPS.

Adv Arendse: So it was around the contract?

Mr Matlala: Yes.

Adv Arendse: By then we know that you had already been awarded the contract, is that right? But your complaint was you were not getting purchase orders.

Mr Matlala: Yes.

Adv Arendse: We do know – I think you can confirm – that you were paid a substantial amount of money before the contract was cancelled.

Mr Matlala: In January?

Adv Arendse: Yes.

Mr Matlala: Yes.

Adv Arendse: And certainly that was a huge amount, I think in the region of R48 million.

Mr Matlala: No, that is not true.

Adv Arendse: Or is that the total amount that you were paid?

Mr Matlala: In January they paid me I think I would say between R10 and R14 million.

Adv Arendse: So R200 000 was that small change for you?

Mr Matlala: No, I am not saying that.

Adv Arendse: Did you go to Beverly Hills with the R200 000? Was it again in a Woollies bag or was it in some other, maybe a checkers or shop right bag?

Mr Matlala: We always operate with Woollies bag\[s\].

Adv Arendse: Again?

Mr Matlala: Yes.

Adv Arendse: Your favourite bag?

Mr Matlala: Yes, that is the money bag.

Adv Arendse: Again, how did you access that cash? Did you come to Beverly Hills with the R200 000?

Mr Matlala: Yes.

Adv Arendse: Where was that money withdrawn from and how and who?

Mr Matlala: The same process from the bank in Pretoria.

Adv Arendse: And it was again your colleague, the director of the company?

Mr Matlala: Yes.

Adv Arendse: So this time you travelled with R200 000?

Mr Matlala: Yes.

Adv Arendse: And did you drive or fly?

Mr Matlala: I drove.

Adv Arendse: Were you alone?

Mr Matlala: No.

Adv Arendse: Who accompanied you?

Mr Matlala: My protectors.

Adv Arendse: Just the two of you?

Mr Matlala: Not two. I think there were fourteen or sixteen. I do not remember.

Adv Arendse: Fourteen or sixteen?

Police officials do not publicise every meeting that they have with a suspect, routine investigative engagement, and covered by confidentiality, or political reporting. I think you know that. To publicise such meetings would have compromised the informants, exposed investigative methodology, undermine parallel inquiries, allow suspects to map out investigate strategy. That is what Mkhwanazi will tell us when he comes back. The conclusion of that meeting you had there was no corruption there which transpired. Do you agree?

Mr Matlala: There was a suggestion of corruption.

Mr Skosana: But there was no corruption?

Mr Matlala: Technically, there was. He was suggesting I need to work with General Nkhuoa.

Mr Skosana: If someone suggests someone to you, is that corruption?

Mr Matlala: Yeah, but when you tell me that ‘This person they have been paying her. For you to get your things sorted you also need to pay him this much.’ Is that not corruption?

Mr Skosana: Is there credible evidence she is corrupt?

Mr Matlala: He backed \[it\] up by saying she has property she cannot afford. Unless he was lying to me about that. He even gave me an address of one property, which I went to check it out and even took the pictures. If that property belongs to her, meaning she was not lying to me.

Mr Skosana: There was a favour or there was no favour on you by General Mkhwanazi?

Mr Matlala: There was no favour.

Mr Skosana: Any influence besides the issue of Lieutenant-General Nkhuoa?

Mr Matlala: There is nothing.

Mr Skosana: No consignment of any of your cases you are finding now?

Mr Matlala: I did not have cases when I was with him.

Mr Skosana: No contradiction?

Mr Matlala: Meaning that we did not agree on something?

Mr Skosana: Yes.

Mr Matlala: Yes, I did not agree on the fact that if I did not do what he wanted he will charge me for attempted murder.

Mr Skosana: I think for me, the investigation proceeded to the arrest of you. Hence we are here today. Am I right?

Mr Matlala: Yes, but I do not know what led him to do that.

Mr Skosana: Who is Jermaine?

Mr Matlala: He has been convicted for impersonating people using voice manipulation technology, and identity manipulation. He paid a fine for that.

Mr Skosana: And your historical relationship?

Mr Matlala: I do not have a historical relationship with him.

Mr Skosana: Do you know Paul O’Sullivan?

Mr Matlala: Yes, I know him.

Mr Skosana: What is your relationship with him?

Mr Matlala: I do not have a relationship \[with him\]. I know him as a forensic investigator.

Mr Skosana: Did you ever have a meeting with him?

Mr Matlala: I have never met him.

Mr Skosana: Do you have his number?

Mr Matlala: No, I do not have \[it\].

Mr Skosana: Brown Mogotsi, is he your friend?

Mr Matlala: No, he is not a friend.

Mr Skosana: He is the one I said impersonated himself as one of the ministerial staff. Am I right?

Mr Matlala: Yes.

Mr Skosana: You said you paid him how much?

Mr Matlala: I will say between R150 000 and R200 000.

Mr Skosana: For the January 8 \[Statement\]?

Mr Matlala: Yes.

Mr Skosana: You promised us the names of those who travelled – you paid for their travel arrangements. Am I right?

Mr Matlala: Yes.

Mr Skosana: Do you know the Treasurer-General of the ANC, Gwen Ramokgopa?

Mr Matlala: Yes, I know her.

Mr Skosana: Have you ever funded her?

Mr Matlala: No.

Mr Skosana: There is a picture with you and President Ramaphosa. Is it fabricated?

Mr Matlala: No, there is no picture with me and President Ramaphosa.

Mr Skosana: I will show you.

Chairperson: The grandmother in Swaziland, is paternal or maternal?

Mr Skosana: I do not have a grandmother in Swaziland. Maybe you did not hear me nicely. I said KZN.

Chairperson: Did you not say KZN to Swaziland?

Mr Matlala: No, no, no.

Chairperson: It is fine. Is it maternal or paternal?

Mr Matlala: Maternal.

Chairperson: Your mother is the child of the Dlaminis?

Mr Matlala: My mother’s mother.

Chairperson: Your mother was also born from the Dlaminis.

Mr Matlala: From Matlala.

Chairperson: Matlala where? Waterberg, Capricorn, Sekhukhune?

Mr Matlala: I was raised in Gauteng. I heard \[of\] a place called Phokwane.

Chairperson: It is where your father was born?

Mr Matlala: Yes.

Chairperson: Do you know your relatives there?

Mr Matlala: No, I do not.

Chairperson: Let us move to this matter of Mr Jerry Boshoga. What do you mean by the manufacturing of narcotics?

Mr Matlala: To make them. To manufacture them.

Chairperson: Can you explain? Narcotics can be understood in two ways: in the sense of medicine or in the sense of illegal drugs.

Mr Matlala: Illegal drugs, but I do not know the process so I do not know how to explain them.

Chairperson: When you say illegal drugs, you mean he was manufacturing those drugs illegally?

Mr Matlala: Yes.

Chairperson: When did you come to befriend him?

Mr Matlala: I have known him for a very long time, but we just became close, I think two or three years.

Chairperson: When did you come to know that he is manufacturing narcotics?

Mr Matlala: He told me.

Chairperson: When was it?

Mr Matlala: Maybe two years ago.

Chairperson: You lived with that information for the last two years?

Mr Matlala: That is true, yes.

Chairperson: Before you came to depose this information with us have you ever shared it with any person?

Mr Matlala: Yes, I did.

Chairperson: Have you ever shared it with anybody in the authorities of SAPS?

Mr Matlala: No, I did not.

Chairperson: When General Cele says ‘I have been helping you and you are not doing anything’, how did you understand his expectations?

Mr Matlala: That he wanted money.

Chairperson: When you started to give that money, were you describing it as a bribe?

Mr Matlala: As a repayment.

Chairperson: In legal or illegal terms?

Mr Matlala: I would not phrase it as “legal or illegal”.

Chairperson: Why was it not possible for you to do a direct bank transfer?

Mr Matlala: He did not want any transfers. He wanted cash.

Chairperson: What was your understanding in that context when a person does not want to be given money in a manner that is traceable? Did you understand it to be legal or illegal?

Mr Matlala: Illegal.

Chairperson: When there is a case that has been opened with IPID and the case is opened against General Mkhwanazi. You eventually meet, and then he says ‘I will try and help you, but I will also want you to talk to these people to withdraw their case.’ You say one of the victims lost his vocal chords?

Mr Matlala: Yes, that is true.

Chairperson: Did you not understand his action to be interfering with witnesses?

Mr Matlala: Yes, it is.

Chairperson: It is an illegal activity.

Mr Matlala: I would say so.

Chairperson: After that, did any of those victims discuss with you ‘But Matlala, this thing is defeating the ends of justice. We think it must be reported to the authorities’?

Mr Matlala: Yeah, but I did not have any reason to report it to the authorities.

Chairperson: One of those victims did they not think of reporting the matter of interference with the witnesses to the authorities?

Mr Matlala: No, they did not.

Chairperson: Do you still hold to that pillar of honesty and integrity?

Mr Matlala: Yes, I do.

Chairperson: How do you explain these activities that shroud your honesty and integrity? You know a person who manufactures drugs, you know about payments that are done which cannot be traceable, you know activities about defeating the ends of justice.

Mr Matlala: I will say I am striving to be an honest man, but there will be some challenges. I am not a perfect man.

Chairperson: You want us to understand that you are not a perfect man?

Mr Matlala: I am not a perfect person.

Chairperson: You spoke about General Nkhuoa. When you mentioned her name you said ‘If people have a problem with me associating with these other characters, what do you say about this one who attends an event of a metropolitan executive.’ Did I hear you correctly?

Mr Matlala: Yes.

Chairperson: Were you saying it was wrong?

Mr Matlala: That is a client of SAPS and she is an end-user of that contract.

Chairperson: You are saying there could have been a conflict of interest?

Mr Matlala: I am saying if it was me it would be a very different story.

Chairperson: Maybe your suspicions might have been informed that you have been tipped that she is probably a beneficiary from the contracts that happened in the department with the previous service provider.

Mr Matlala: I knew that before that.

Chairperson: You had always known it?

Mr Matlala: The information I had it when I hired Brigadier Lenono. She is the one who gave me the information.

Chairperson: Even before General Mkhwanazi told you, you already knew?

Mr Matlala: Yes.

Chairperson: This information that you have, that there is this employee of SAPS who happens to have a relationship with a service provider in the department, did you see it as an act of illegality?

Mr Matlala: I do not think I am the only one who knows about it. Even Hon Sangoni said she knew about that thing.

Ms Sangoni: I said I was at the wedding. I was asking about her being at the wedding, is that a corrupt act.

Chairperson: This case that you are dealing with now, your greatest conviction is that you are a victim of circumstances?

Mr Matlala: Yes.

Chairperson: And it emanates from you having refused to accede to certain demands?

Mr Matlala: Yes, that is correct.

Chairperson: The many other cases that you would have been charged \[with\] previously, do you hold the same view that you could have been hounded?

Mr Matlala: No, I am not saying that.

Chairperson: If you were one day to be called to share with us what you know, would you gladly welcome that?

Mr Matlala: Yes, I will.

Chairperson: Will you not think it is a witch hunt if someone wants to bring someone from 2009?

Mr Matlala: I would not say that. It depends on what motivates that.

Chairperson: If such cases were to be brought back, would you say ‘I have now been given an opportunity to clear my name’?

Mr Matlala: I have already cleared my name, hence they were withdrawn.

Chairperson: In some cases you were acquitted, in some cases they were withdrawn. Somebody says ‘No, these cases must be reinstated’. What would be your reaction?

Mr Matlala: I will have to clear my name.

Chairperson: We want to thank you for your time.

The meeting was adjourned.

CORRUPTION NEWS

# Matlala: cash bribes to Cele, threats from Mkhwanazi during SAPS contract woes

By Corruption Watch 28 Nov 2025, 10:49

**Getting your [Trinity Audio](//trinityaudio.ai) player ready...**

The parliamentary [ad hoc committee](https://pmg.org.za/committee/391/) investigating allegations of police corruption [has heard](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=n-_J3FCuDLQ) how Vusimuzi “Cat” Matlala solicited help from all fronts in relation to his business with the South African Police Service (SAPS) and the alleged harassment by the political killings task team (PKTT). Matlala approached former police minister Bheki Cele, suspended deputy national commissioner Lieutenant-General Shadrack Sibiya, and KwaZulu-Natal (KZN) provincial police commissioner Lieutenant-General Nhlanhla Mkhwanazi, he said.

Matlala is at the centre of a controversial, but short-lived, tender that is under investigation for alleged irregularities. His company Medicare24 won a R360-million contract in July 2024 to provide medical and wellness services for members of the SAPS at its college in Pretoria. He told [the committee](https://www.parliament.gov.za/ad-hoc-committee-gen-mkhwanazis-allegations) that based on this, he was targeted for extortion and frustrated with technicalities in an effort to get him to bankroll SAPS senior officials. While this was going on, he also became a person of interest for the PKTT, which was probing the kidnapping of businessman Jerry Boshoga.

#### Business with the SAPS

Matlala first leased a healthcare facility on the premises of the SAPS Pretoria college in 2022. He denied it when questioned whether this move was in anticipation of securing the lucrative tender two years later. In January 2024, he said, he met Sibiya when he approached him for assistance with facilitating the eviction of medical staff who continued to occupy the facility despite the previous contract having ended. Sibiya was the acting national police commissioner at the time while national commissioner Major-General Fannie Masemola was on leave.  

His troubles worsened, over the next few months, following the award of the contract. Over time he noticed that he was not getting the cooperation he relied on from Lieutenant-General Lineo Nkhuoa, SAPS head of human resources. As the end user of Medicare24’s services, Nkhuoa was expected to facilitate the furnishing of purchase orders associated with the project, but was not forthcoming with these, and this in turn delayed payments to Medicare24.

While this was going on, there was also a police investigation into the Boshoga case, culminating in the raid of Matlala’s home in Pretoria on 6 December 2024. On this occasion, he claims, his family was harassed and several firearms belonging to his other business, Cat VIP Security, were confiscated by balaclava-wearing PKTT members. The next raid happened at his Cat VIP business premises, leading him to finally take action to address what he deemed as harassment.

#### **Help** solicited

When his efforts to get this sorted out were not successful, help came from several quarters, one of them being a suggestion from a friend, Bongani Mpungose, who facilitated a meeting with Cele in Durban. Upon telling the former minister of his troubles, Matlala believes Cele phoned the head of crime intelligence Lieutenant-General Dumisani Khumalo, who is also the project lead of the PKTT. He overheard Cele say over the phone that he (Matlala) was caught up in a “Zulu war” that had nothing to do with him. The inference he drew from this was that Cele was probably referring to the PKTT being operated by Khumalo, with Mkhwanazi also being involved as it originated in his province and there were factional fights in senior SAPS circles over the task team.

After the call, Matlala was then told by Cele that the matter was resolved and that he could fetch his firearms from the Brooklyn police station, where they had been kept. For his troubles, Cele was given the first tranche of cash totalling R300 000. Mpungose was also paid, although Matlala did not disclose the amount given to him.

Cele would receive R200 000 on one more occasion, while also enjoying other favours from Matlala including accommodation at his upmarket apartment in Menlyn and transportation around Gauteng when his family was in the province. Matlala told the committee that he characterised Cele as an extortionist because he would always call him when he needed money – naming his price as R1-million – and when he decided to stop bankrolling him, he believes the punishment was the arrest in May 2025 for the attempted murder of his former girlfriend, Tebogo Thobejane.

Cele would also later facilitate a meeting with Mkhwanazi at which Matlala would ask for help with his challenges. He said he met Mkhwanazi at The Pearls in Umhlanga early in 2025, with KZN head of the Directorate for Priority Crimes Investigations, Major-General Lesetja Senona, in tow. Matlala said he wanted Senona – who has been implicated in the Madlanga commission for helping to facilitate the award of the contract to Matlala and for frustrating the PKTT’s investigations – because they have a close relationship.

At this meeting, Mkhwanazi promised to intervene on Matlala’s behalf, but warned him that Nkhuoa was corrupt and relentless in demanding kickbacks from service providers. He also made a veiled threat, according to Matlala, that he could “take him out” if he ever crossed him. When questioned about what Mkhwanazi got in return for his offer of help, Matlala said he expected nothing. A proposition was later made to Matlala that Mkhwanazi may have played him on this occasion, which proposition he accepted.

The other source of help, also in December, came in the form of North West businessman Brown Mogotsi, who called Matlala and identified himself as working in the office of suspended police minister Senzo Mchunu. Mogotsi offered to help Matlala with his PKTT woes as well as with the contract, which was under scrutiny at this point and on the verge of being cancelled. Mogotsi repeatedly suggested that the Independent Police Investigative Directorate be roped in to address the harassment claims that Matlala had made, to help get the PKTT off his back.

Mogotsi was also meant to facilitate a meeting with Mchunu to discuss the matter of the contract, but this never happened, according to Matlala. Trusting his promises of help, however, Matlala paid a total of around R150 000 to Mogotsi on several occasions. When Mogotsi promised to secure a team of investigators to probe the 6 December incident, he told Matlala that because they were not Gauteng-based, they would have to be accommodated. Furthermore, Mogotsi expected Matlala to finance the transportation and accommodation of a group of the former’s associates who would attend the ANC’s 8 January celebration in Khayelitsha, Cape Town.

It would soon become apparent to Matlala, however, that the transactional relationship was one sided, and that Mogotsi was failing to keep his end of the bargain. As did Cele, he stopped payments to Mogotsi.

“I would say Cele is an extortionist and Mogotsi is a con artist,” said Matlala.

The veracity of Matlala’s evidence was tested on numerous occasions during his testimony, with a common theme of him being motivated by revenge for both his incarceration and the cancellation of his contract.

#### Villain or victim?

The topic of Matlala’s background and upbringing also came up during the questioning by committee members. He replied that he was born and raised in Mamelodi by a single mother who later disappeared from his life following a traumatic experience of sexual assault, leading him to be homeless for a large part of his youth. After completing matric, which is his highest level of education, he started “selling goods” to support himself. He acknowledged his extensive rap sheet as pointed out by members, saying that it did not preclude him from seeking business opportunities that include tenders with government.

He denied that he was involved in the drug trade, despite admitting that Jerry Boshoga, with whom he shares a close friendship, is himself a drug dealer. In fact, Matlala testified that he learned from Boshoga’s brother that on the day of his alleged kidnapping, the two of them had gone to collect large containers of a drug-manufacturing ingredient. When questioned on the implications of this kind of friendship on his moral standing, Matlala said he lives by a principle of not judging how other people around him live.

He was further questioned on his lavish lifestyle and said he maintains it with his legitimate businesses after years of living a life of crime. His previous conviction for the possession of stolen goods in the early 2000s was one of the grounds on which Matlala was denied bail after his arrest. He told the committee, however, that he believes that there is more to it than that, and that he is being targeted by influential individuals who want him to suffer for refusing to share the spoils of his tender.

Proof of this, he added, was that the contract had gone back to Metropolitan, the company that held it for years before him. He said it was no coincidence that Nkhuoa attended the wedding of one of Metropolitan’s directors after the reinstatement of its relationship with the SAPS.

“If that had been me, there would be trouble. But because it is their darling, no-one is saying anything,” Matlala said.

Even the police officers who have been investigating him have fabricated evidence to his detriment, he added. The recording played at the Madlanga commission in October during the testimonies of in-camera witnesses who are the investigators in his case, he said, was manipulated to sound real when it actually never happened. In it, the investigators claim Matlala confessed to having bribed Sibiya with R80 000 to help pay for his son’s engagement party, in return for his help.

Matlala told the committee that his only crime was that he did not submit to demands from certain quarters of the SAPS to maintain kickbacks.

Committee chairperson Soviet Lekganyane announced at the end of proceedings that Matlala was the last witness to be heard for this year, and that the committee would resume its hearings in the new year owing to an extension of its term granted by the Office of the Speaker of Parliament.

# Some of my business dealings were unethical but not unlawful: Matlala

![](https://www.sabcnews.com/sabcnews/wp-content/uploads/2025/11/Cat-Matlala-2.jpg)

*   'Cat' Matlala appearing before Ad Hoc Committee

*   Image Credits :
*   SABC News

Abongwe Kobokana

*   27 November 2025, 16:29 \[SAST\]

[](https://www.facebook.com/sharer/sharer.php?u=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.sabcnews.com%2Fsabcnews%2F1086035-2%2F "Facebook")[](https://twitter.com/intent/tweet?text=Some%20of%20my%20business%20dealings%20were%20unethical%20but%20not%20unlawful%3A%20Matlala&url=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.sabcnews.com%2Fsabcnews%2F1086035-2%2F "X")[](https://api.whatsapp.com/send?text=Some%20of%20my%20business%20dealings%20were%20unethical%20but%20not%20unlawful%3A%20Matlala%20https%3A%2F%2Fwww.sabcnews.com%2Fsabcnews%2F1086035-2%2F "Whatsapp")[](https://www.linkedin.com/sharing/share-offsite/?url=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.sabcnews.com%2Fsabcnews%2F1086035-2%2F "Linkedin")

Businessman and alleged criminal cartel kingpin Vusimuzi “Cat” Matlala has refuted statements that his business empire has been achieved through unlawful means.

Matlala however, admitted that some of his businesses can be described as unethical but not unlawful.

[He was grilled by evidence leader, Advocate Norman Arendse.](https://www.sabcnews.com/sabcnews/matlala-claims-former-police-minister-cele-acquired-money-from-him/)

“I have got letters here. I don’t think you have got these statements. But I will share them with you. But I have been sending letters demanding that I am not being paid. Why am I not getting any work anymore? So, this thing is frustrating. So, this is out of frustration? You pursuit lawful avenues to have whatever is left in your contract to have that unblocked by whatever was blocking you. So, you would rather to get involved to unlawful activities to unlock it. I would say it was not unlawful at that time. I would say it unethical.”

Meanwhile earlier, Matlala accused police of manipulating evidence in his cellphone. He says this is in order to plant evidence on it.

“The attempted murder has nothing to do with these messages. Why do you think they will go to all this extent to manipulate your phone? They did it to plant evidence. And I am assuming SC you will tell us which is this evident you believe has been planted in your phone? Yes.”
